findings.title: Disk-full errors are downgraded to per-member failures
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1146 routes shard write errors into the new fold, and lines 1204-1207 contain every error accepted by failure_is_containable. However, lines 193-205 recognize only ReadOnlyFilesystem and EROFS/ERROR_WRITE_PROTECT; ENOSPC/StorageFull and Windows ERROR_DISK_FULL are not classified as volume-level. transfer_session/mod.rs:4646-4648 then allows these contained failures through for mirrors.
findings.predicted_failure: When a destination fills during a tar shard, remaining members continue being attempted and the mirror completes as a contained partial transfer instead of failing the session. At this landed slice, the mirror can exit successfully without a failure summary despite an incomplete backup.
findings.better_approach: Treat StorageFull and platform disk-full/quota codes as volume-unwritable, with guards covering shard and single-file paths.

findings.title: Deferred rayon classification can miss a dead destination root
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1046-1053 and 1065-1116 collect every rayon result before classification; only later, at lines 1204-1207, does the fold call failure_is_containable. destination_root_live at lines 175-181 therefore observes root state after all workers finish, not when each error occurred.
findings.predicted_failure: If an SMB root disconnects during member writes and reconnects before rayon collection finishes, or the root is otherwise recreated, errors caused by the dead root are reclassified as per-file failures. The mirror can finish incomplete rather than producing the required session-fatal destination-root error.
findings.better_approach: Classify each member error immediately in its worker and fold a preserved fatal-versus-contained classification afterward.
